name: LP-AM13E230 LaunchPad development kit
sources: AM13E230x data sheet SPRSPC3A (Rev. A, ADVANCE INFORMATION, revised August 2026; features, TMU, NPU, flash wait states); LaunchPad user guide SLVUDH9 (March 2026; Tables 2-1 to 2-11, Figure 1-1 board, Figure 2-9 header pinout, Rev E1 and E2 appendices); TI product and tool pages; AM13E2x SDK 26.01.00.03.STS on this Mac. All read 2026-10-07.

columns.head: The chip: AM13E23019
items: 200 MHz on this board (data sheet allows 250 MHz), floating-point unit, DSP instructions, custom datapath extension
Two 256 kB banks. 3 wait states at 200 MHz, with a prefetch buffer and cache
96 kB for data plus 32 kB tuned for running code
Data sheet: 225 µA per MHz running CoreMark, 196 µA in STANDBY

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: A trig unit (sin, cos, atan, divide, square root in a few cycles) and a TinyEngine neural accelerator, 600 to 1,200 million operations a second
6 outputs each, with dead band and trip inputs: built to drive a three-phase motor
Three 12-bit converters, 7.81 million samples a second, triggered by the PWM
Fast over-current trips; two have a DAC that can drive a pin

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: Isolated XDS110 debug probe, CAN-FD transceiver, 5 V encoder header, red and green LEDs, wake and BSL buttons, 25 MHz crystal, power-measurement header J10
40-pin BoosterPack (J1 to J4); motor BoosterPacks plug straight on
No motor driver and no motor: the BoosterPack and motor were not bought. No EnergyTrace named in the user guide
Prototype silicon (XAM13E23019) and a pre-release SDK. Rev E1 boards have different pins: look for MCU178E1 on the back
